cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For Normal (eGFR >=90), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For Mild (eGFR 60-89), the starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2]. For Moderate (eGFR 30-59), the starting dose is 25 mg OD, maximum is 50 mg/day, and monitoring is recheck 2-4 weeks [E2, E3]; the approved German renal starting dose for moderate renal impairment is 25 mg once daily [E1]. For Severe (eGFR 15-29), the starting dose is specialist review, maximum is 25 mg/day, and monitoring is enhanced [E2].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 versus control are: nausea 12.7 % versus 6.0 % (Serious? No), headache 14.0 % versus 6.6 % (Serious? No), fatigue 15.3 % versus 7.2 % (Serious? No), dizziness 16.6 % versus 7.8 % (Serious? No), rash 17.8 % versus 8.4 % (Serious? No), and transaminase elevation 19.1 % versus 9.0 % (Serious? Yes) [E1]. In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 versus control are: nausea 11.8 % versus 6.0 % (Serious? No), headache 13.0 % versus 6.6 % (Serious? No), fatigue 14.2 % versus 7.2 % (Serious? No), dizziness 15.4 % versus 7.8 % (Serious? No), rash 16.6 % versus 8.4 % (Serious? No), and transaminase elevation 17.7 % versus 9.0 % (Serious? Yes) [E2]. The structured data verifies these values [E3]. For HN-204, the highest treatment % is transaminase elevation (19.1) [E4]. For HN-311, the highest treatment % is transaminase elevation (17.7) [E4]. Treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) are: dizziness -1.2 points, fatigue -1.1 points, headache -1.0 points, nausea -0.9 points, rash -1.2 points, and transaminase elevation -1.4 points [E4]. Control % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) are +0.0 points for all events [E4].
